analysis.investment_thesis: Wakefit fails the Magic Formula on both legs — EBIT is negative (−₹5 Cr in FY25), making earnings yield uncalculable, while ROCE of −1.05% confirms zero return on capital. At EV/EBITDA of 54.9x for a company that has never turned a net profit, the market is pricing perfection into a fundamentally broken business.
key_strengths: Revenue compounding at ~26% CAGR (₹797 Cr → ₹1,256 Cr in 2 years) shows genuine demand
EBITDA improved significantly from −₹87 Cr (FY23) to +₹83 Cr (FY25), showing path toward profitability
Gross margin of 54% is healthy for a consumer goods brand, suggesting pricing power
key_risks: EBIT is negative (−₹5 Cr FY25) — Magic Formula cannot even be applied; no earnings yield to speak of
Net losses deepened in FY25 (−₹35 Cr) versus FY24 (−₹15 Cr) despite higher revenue — cost structure is worsening
Debt nearly doubled to ₹273 Cr while cash collapsed to ₹7 Cr; leverage rising as profitability stays elusive
red_flags: Negative EBIT in 2 of 3 years — Magic Formula disqualifies this company outright
P/E of 118x is internally inconsistent with reported net losses of −₹35 Cr — data quality or accounting adjustment concern
Free cash flow collapsed from ₹52 Cr (FY24) to ₹26 Cr (FY25) despite capex only at ₹51 Cr — operating quality deteriorating
Promoter holding of only 37% in a founder-led consumer brand is relatively low; no insider conviction signal
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, Wakefit is uninvestable at this stage. The formula requires positive EBIT to compute earnings yield (EBIT/EV), and Wakefit's FY25 EBIT of −₹5 Cr (operating income) fails this basic screen. Even using EBITDA of ₹83 Cr, the EV/EBITDA of 54.9x implies an EBITDA yield of ~1.8% — far below the 12–15% earnings yield threshold that makes a stock attractive. ROCE of −1.05% confirms capital is being destroyed, not compounded, and the ROE of −6.72% tells the same story. This is a business spending heavily to grow revenues without generating returns above the cost of capital.

The trajectory has some optionality — EBITDA went from −₹87 Cr to +₹83 Cr in two years, and revenue is scaling well. But the net loss worsened in FY25 (−₹35 Cr vs. −₹15 Cr in FY24), debt has ballooned to ₹273 Cr against ₹7 Cr cash, and FCF halved year-over-year. Greenblatt's framework rewards businesses with durable high returns on tangible capital bought at cheap prices — Wakefit offers neither. At a market cap of ₹4,905 Cr on ₹1,256 Cr revenue with no net profit history, investors are paying a steep price for an uncertain promise of future earnings. Pass.
